controls.title: Submitter, department, accountable owner, and executive sponsor are identified.
The problem or opportunity and current process are documented.
Affected users, expected benefit, and baseline measures are documented.
Expected technology, integrations, data sources, ownership, and sensitivity are identified.
Initial governance, security, data, application, network, vendor, and adoption risks are captured.
AI is documented as an appropriate option to evaluate.
The intake is sufficiently complete for qualification.
High-level technical and organizational feasibility are assessed.
Costs, expected benefits, and value assumptions are assessed.
An initial AI and technical risk assessment is completed.
Required Cyber, Data, Application, Network, and Enterprise reviews are identified.
Initial risks can be mitigated within acceptable limits or are escalated.
The business case is proportionate to the identified risk.
The proceed, reject, or return-for-information decision is recorded.
Business value, feasibility, and gravity are scored using approved criteria.
Technical feasibility and architecture fit are confirmed.
Platform, infrastructure, integration, and licensing availability are confirmed.
Data availability, ownership, quality, and access feasibility are assessed.
Delivery capacity, required expertise, schedule, and budget are assessed.
The buy, build, configure, or reuse decision is recorded.
Priority and sequencing decisions are recorded.
Backlog or deferral rationale is recorded when the use case is not selected.
A cross-functional delivery team and accountable technical owners are assigned.
Current-state and proposed solution architecture, components, environments, and trust boundaries are documented.
Data sources, classification, ownership, lineage, quality, retention, residency, and permitted uses are documented.
Data flows, retrieval sources, storage locations, transformations, and downstream consumers are documented.
Authentication, authorization, service accounts, secrets, privileged access, and least-privilege controls are defined.
Network connectivity, segmentation, firewall rules, ingress, egress, DNS, certificates, proxies, and external endpoints are reviewed.
APIs, integrations, dependencies, interface contracts, error handling, and environment separation are documented.
Model, prompt, agent, retrieval, grounding, output-validation, user-interface, and human-oversight requirements are defined.

Technical and AI risks are assessed for security, data exposure, prompt injection, unauthorized retrieval, hallucination, poisoning, unsafe automation, vendor change, reliability, and model degradation.
Preventive, detective, and corrective controls are mapped to each material technical risk, with control owners and target dates.
Logging, auditability, observability, alerting, incident escalation, and operational ownership are defined.
Availability, capacity, scalability, recovery, fallback, rollback, and business-continuity requirements are documented.
Success measures, technical acceptance criteria, monitoring indicators, thresholds, and review cadence are defined.
Cyber, Data, Application, Network, and Enterprise reviews are completed or formally marked not applicable, and implementation approval is recorded.
Business testers are identified and required tool training is completed.
Data is acquired, processed, documented, versioned, and access-controlled as designed.
Training, validation, and test datasets are separated when applicable.
Models, prompts, agents, integrations, configurations, dependencies, and guardrails are version controlled.
Identity, security, data, network, and application controls from the approved design are implemented.
Outputs are validated in the intended operational context.
Trustworthy AI characteristics and human-oversight controls are evaluated.
Vendor development, model, dependency, and assurance evidence is reviewed when applicable.
The solution and supporting evidence are ready for structured testing.
Test requirements, acceptance criteria, datasets, scripts, and expected outcomes are approved.
Developer, integration, performance, failure-mode, and recovery testing is completed.
Cybersecurity, identity, access, logging, vulnerability, and abuse-case testing is completed.
Data protection, retrieval authorization, quality, leakage, retention, and lineage controls are tested.
Prompt injection, hallucination, unsafe output, grounding, guardrail, and human-oversight controls are tested.
Business users are trained and user-acceptance testing is completed.
Defects and findings are triaged, assigned, remediated, and retested.
A production pilot is approved and completed when required.
Pilot results, user feedback, limitations, and unresolved risks are documented.
Required reviewers confirm that approval conditions have been satisfied or carried forward.
The deploy, remediate, pause, or stop decision is recorded.
Final user training, communications, and change-readiness activities are completed.
Production identity, access, network, data, application, and security configurations are verified.
Monitoring, logging, alerting, escalation, and operational ownership are active.
Rollback, recovery, service interruption, and deployment-incident procedures are documented and tested.
Production stability, capacity, support readiness, and dependency availability are confirmed.
Trustworthy AI deployment controls and human-oversight responsibilities are confirmed.
The inventory, technical risk register, approvals, evidence, and known limitations are current.
The deployment decision, release date, conditions, and accountable authority are recorded.
User feedback and reported limitations are reviewed on the approved cadence.
Data access, consumption, quality, lineage, retention, and unauthorized retrieval are monitored.
Cost, licensing, infrastructure, model, and platform consumption are monitored.
Availability, latency, capacity, reliability, and network performance are monitored against thresholds.
Accuracy, grounding, fairness, safety, and other approved AI measures are reviewed.
Model, prompt, agent, dependency, vendor, API, and platform changes are assessed before adoption.
Exceptions and incidents are linked to structured issues, corrective actions, and evidence.
Residual risks, approval conditions, and expiring exceptions are reviewed.
The continue, improve, pause, or close decision is recorded.
The closure reason, final decision, decision authority, and effective date are recorded.
Contractual, vendor, licensing, data, and retention commitments are identified.
Downstream users, integrations, dependencies, and service impacts are identified.
Replacement, transition, rollback, or continuity plans are completed when required.
Affected users, data owners, reviewers, and governance stakeholders are notified.
Data retention, deletion, records, and audit obligations are completed and evidenced.
Accounts, access, secrets, licenses, integrations, network paths, and production resources are removed.
Final outcomes, realized benefits, unresolved obligations, and lessons learned are documented.
Decommissioning is independently verified and the inventory is closed.
